cast.name: Isaura Ombrecht
cast.role: Master Wright of the Greyfall yard and head of the Ombrecht rope-making family; refuses to certify ropes kept past seven years, loses her guild seal, and ends as Pass-keeper at Greyfall

cast.name: Tobiah Ombrecht
cast.role: foreman of the Greyfall brake sheds, Isaura's son and Linnet's father; takes the Syndicate's retainer in Year five and bars his brake house against a ghost run in Year eight

cast.name: Linnet Ombrecht
cast.role: apprentice and later Chief Wright of Greyfall, the only Ombrecht with the ear for ropes (the Ombrecht note); the book is told mostly through her eyes

cast.name: Dessa Varnholt
cast.role: dispatcher at Greyfall and keeper of the Book; wrote Mark on the morning of the runaway and later leaks the Commissioner's memo

cast.name: Rurik Sennet
cast.role: brake inspector at Greyfall and Dessa's partner at the second key; passed the brake band before the runaway, refuses to ride a car again, and walks to Ostrel to give evidence

cast.name: Calla Reth
cast.role: chief hydrographer at Tarn House (Dr. Reth), the researcher who measures the retreat of Old Mara and predicts the date of Low Day

cast.name: Emeric Haldric
cast.role: Commissioner of the HWC; shelves Calla's report, issues the Weight Cuts and the confidential memo, and resigns in Year seven

cast.name: Jessamy Tolk
cast.role: the Sill Freight Syndicate's night broker, who runs ghost cars and lends Tobiah money; becomes Night Warden of the Ladder after the Reconciliation

terms.definition: the chain of seven cableways that is the only way up to Ostrel
the steel tank under a car that is its water ballast; holds ninety barrels when filled to the Mark
the ring of white paint inside a belly that fixes the most water it may take
the great iron wheel in the upper station that the haul-rope loops over and the brakes act on
the margin by which the heavy car outweighs the light one; a line moves only while it is positive
the stone channel that carries a drained belly's water down to the top station of the next line
the unit of weight equal to one barrel of water
the number of tallies a line lifts in a working day
the twice-daily reading of the lake's level, telegraphed to every dispatcher
haul-rope of twelve steel strands braided around a core of treated sedge fibre
the short stretch of double track in the middle of every line where the two cars meet
the full minute both cars halt at the Pass on every run while the keeper listens to the rope
a line may not start until the dispatcher's key and the inspector's key are turned in the same minute
the first day of every month, when freight outranks passengers
the Highline Water Commission, which owns the water and employs the dispatchers, inspectors, weighers and hydrographers
the Sill Freight Syndicate, the grain carters' consortium at Pannock that sells ghost cars
a run made outside the dispatcher's book, usually after the dusk bell, with water taken from a tailrace before its proper turn
a hidden pipe tapped into a tailrace and plugged with a wooden bung
the day in the dry stretch of the year when the Brimmer is lowest, which moves earlier as the glacier shrinks
May to September, when Old Mara is running and the Brimmer is topped daily
the Year two rationing circular that cut the permitted runs on every line by a sixth
the Year two circular that raised the working life of a haul-rope from seven years to nine
the feeder channel that brings the springs of the eastern pastures to the top of the Third Line
the Fourth to Seventh Lines, which run only sixteen weeks of the Fill Season after the Reconciliation

timeline.label: forty-one years before Year one
timeline.event: the Seventh Line opens, completing the Ladder, and the HWC is chartered

timeline.label: sixty years before Year one
timeline.event: the First Line opens (the Ladder took nineteen years to finish)

timeline.label: twenty-nine years before Year one
timeline.event: the Sill Freight Syndicate is founded by the grain carters of Pannock

timeline.label: forty-seven years before Year one
timeline.event: Isaura goes onto the long walks at fourteen

timeline.label: Year one, February
timeline.event: Calla's stakes show the ice slipping far faster than usual

timeline.label: Year one, May
timeline.event: Tolk visits Tobiah at the Greyfall brake shed; Linnet sees the first ghost car

timeline.label: Year one, September
timeline.event: Low Day falls on the twenty-fourth; Linnet is apprenticed

timeline.label: Year two, March
timeline.event: the Weight Cuts and the seventy-five day brake-band circular

timeline.label: Year two, October
timeline.event: the Fourth Line runs away on Haul Day; eleven people die

timeline.label: Year two, December
timeline.event: the inquiry; then the Extension Order raising rope life from seven years to nine

timeline.label: Year three, February
timeline.event: Isaura refuses to certify the Second Line's rope under the Extension Order

timeline.label: Year three, May
timeline.event: the guild withdraws Isaura's seal; Linnet becomes her ears

timeline.label: Year three, August
timeline.event: Low Day falls on the twenty-seventh; Haldric visits Calla at Tarn House

timeline.label: Year four, March
timeline.event: Linnet hears the Second Line's rope go flat; the guild's load test

timeline.label: Year four, November
timeline.event: Haldric's confidential memorandum to the station chiefs

timeline.label: Year five, July
timeline.event: Tobiah takes the Syndicate's retainer of forty crowns a quarter

timeline.label: Year five, November
timeline.event: Dessa copies the memo and posts it to the Sill Evening Post

timeline.label: Year six, April
timeline.event: Calla's paper On the Retreat of Old Mara is published

timeline.label: Year six, July
timeline.event: Low Day falls on the sixteenth of July, as the table said

timeline.label: Year one, November
timeline.event: the timeline jumps backward: Calla's report to Haldric, filed under Prudence

timeline.label: Year seven, February
timeline.event: Rurik walks to Ostrel and tells the Assembly "I turned the key"

timeline.label: Year seven, September
timeline.event: Haldric resigns; Dessa is released

timeline.label: Year eight, January
timeline.event: Tobiah bars the brake house door against a ghost run

timeline.label: Year nine, June
timeline.event: Low Day on the fourth; the Seventh Line stops on the ninth

timeline.label: Year nine, August
timeline.event: the Reconciliation: the Ketterby Cut, the Summer Ladder, a reformed Commission

rules.text: A belly is never filled past the Mark
No run begins until the dispatcher's key and the inspector's key are turned in the same minute
Both cars halt at the Pass for the Held Minute on every run
A haul-rope is retired after seven years of service, however it looks
No flame is carried within thirty paces of a haul-rope
The seal on the Sluice is broken by the Commissioner or by nobody

inconsistencies.description: The Brimmer is said to hold forty thousand barrels when full in the description of the lake, but sixty thousand barrels when full in the account of Calla's Year one report
Rurik Sennet's profile dates the Fourth Line runaway to the October of Year three, but the chronology (and the Year two, December inquiry that follows it) dates it to Year two, October

questions.ask: How many barrels of water does a belly hold when it is filled to the Mark?
What is sedgewire made of, and how many steel strands does it have?
How many years did it take to finish building the Ladder?
How old was Rurik Sennet in Year one, and what was his job?
How much was the retainer Tobiah took from the Syndicate, and when did he take it?
How many people died when the Fourth Line ran away?
On what date did Low Day fall in Year one?
What do the letters SFS stand for, and who founded it?
Who is this story about, and what does each of the main people do in it?
How does the story end up for the Ladder and for the main people?
What are the rules of this world, and how do the characters bend them?
What is the central problem in the story, how does it build up step by step, and where does it end?
How does a line lift freight up the mountain, and where does its water come from and go? Walk me through it.
When was the Commissioner's memo written, and when did it leak out?
Where does the timeline jump backward, and to what moment does it go back?
How did the date of Low Day change between Year one and Year six?
Which came first: Isaura losing her seal, or Linnet hearing the Second Line's rope go flat?
What point of view and tense is this bible written in?
How does the memo differ in register from the rest of the bible?
How much of the bible is dialogue, and what is it like?
How is the bible organised from beginning to end?
The bible says how much water the Brimmer holds when it is full. Does it say the same thing everywhere?
Does the bible give the same year for the Fourth Line runaway in the character notes and in the dated entries?
Is the bible consistent about when Isaura lost her guild seal? Check the cast notes against the dated entries.
New idea for the book: what if the Pass-keeper at Greyfall could be paid to cut the Held Minute short on certain nights? I think it adds a nice complication. Does that fit what I have?
I had an idea for the last act: Linnet starts to lose her hearing. Could that work with how I've set her up?
What if Haldric had a sister in Pannock who runs a bakery, so the bread prices hit her family? Is that useful for his character?
Idea: someone moves Calla's stakes on the glacier at night, and I'm thinking the Syndicate is behind it. Does that make sense with what I've set up?
